rows.stem: Which of the following is an example of endothermic process ?

options.label: B
options.text: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost

options.label: C
options.text: Dissolution of ammonium chloride in water

options.label: D
options.text: Digestion of food in our body

rows.solution:
An endothermic process absorbs heat. When ammonium chloride dissolves in water, the solution becomes cold because heat is taken in from the surroundings, so the process is endothermic.

Forming slaked lime from quicklime and water gives out a lot of heat, and decomposition of vegetable matter into compost and digestion of food (with respiration) also release energy. These are exothermic.

This is option (C) Dissolution of ammonium chloride in water.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
In the given experimental set-up, if the experiment is carried out separately with each of the following solutions the cases in which the bulb will glow is/are :

(i) Dilute hydrochloric acid

(ii) Dilute sulphuric acid

(iii) Glucose solution

(iv) Alcohol
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the standard conductivity set-up: a beaker labelled 'Solution' with two nails fixed in a cork dipping into it, wired through a battery, a bulb and a plug key. The solutions are all named in the stem, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
In the set-up the nails dip into the solution and are connected to a battery and a bulb through a plug key. The bulb glows only if the solution conducts electricity.

Dilute hydrochloric acid and dilute sulphuric acid produce \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions in water, and these ions carry the current, so the bulb glows. Glucose and alcohol contain hydrogen but do not give \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions in solution, so they do not conduct and the bulb does not glow.

This is option (C) (i) and (ii).

rows.stem:
In order to balance the following chemical equation, the values of the coefficients x and y respectively are :

\(\mathrm{x\,Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{Heat} 2\,PbO + y\,NO_2 + O_2}\)
rows.solution:
Balance lead first: the right side has 2 PbO, so \(x = 2\). Two \(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2}\) carry 4 nitrogen atoms, so \(y = 4\).

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO + 4NO_2 + O_2}\)

Check oxygen: 12 on the left, and \(2 + 8 + 2 = 12\) on the right.

So x and y are 2 and 4, which is option (A) 2, 4.

rows.stem: When zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide, the product formed is :
rows.solution:
Zinc reacts with hot sodium hydroxide solution to give sodium zincate and hydrogen gas:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\)

This is option (B) Sodium zincate.

rows.subtopic: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
rows.stem: Among the following, the metal with lowest density is :
rows.solution:
Lithium is the lightest metal, with a density of about 0.53 g/cm\(^3\), so light that it floats on water. Magnesium (about 1.7), aluminium (about 2.7) and lead (about 11.3) are all much denser.

This is option (A) Lithium.

rows.stem: The number of electrons in the outermost shell of the atom of a non-metal can be :
rows.solution:
Non-metals usually have 4 to 7 electrons in their outermost shell, and they complete their octet by gaining or sharing electrons. Atoms with 1, 2 or 3 outer electrons are metals, which lose them; an atom with 8 has a complete octet (a noble gas).

Of the choices, the one that fits is option (C) 5, 6 or 7.

rows.stem: The total number of electrons shared in the formation of an ethyne molecule is :
rows.solution:
Ethyne is \(\mathrm{H{-}C{\equiv}C{-}H}\). The two carbon atoms share three pairs of electrons (a triple bond), and each carbon shares one pair with a hydrogen atom.

Shared pairs: \(3 + 1 + 1 = 5\), so the number of shared electrons is \(5 \times 2 = 10\).

This is option (C) 10.

rows.stem: Sphincter muscles are present at the exit of :
rows.solution:
The exit of the stomach into the small intestine is regulated by a sphincter muscle, which releases food into the small intestine a little at a time. The exit of the undigested waste through the anus is regulated by the anal sphincter.

This is option (B) Stomach and anus.

rows.stem: In the following diagram, identify the cells through which massive amounts of gaseous exchange takes place for photosynthesis :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a drawn cross-section of a leaf (an upper cell layer, elongated cells packed with chloroplasts, rounded cells below, a lower cell layer) with four arrows labelled I, II, III and IV pointing at different structures; which structure each label marks is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
In the figure, I marks the upper epidermis, II the elongated cells packed with chloroplasts, III the rounded cells below them, and IV the gap in the lower epidermis, which is a stoma.

Massive amounts of gaseous exchange for photosynthesis (carbon dioxide in, oxygen out) take place through the stomata, the tiny pores on the surface of the leaf.

This is option (B) IV.

rows.stem: During vigorous exercise, the occurrence of cramps in the outer muscles of an athlete is due to the conversion of pyruvate to :
rows.solution:
During vigorous exercise the muscle cells run short of oxygen, and pyruvate is converted to lactic acid (anaerobic respiration in muscle). The build-up of lactic acid causes cramps.

This is option (C) Lactic acid.

rows.stem: Plants which bear unisexual flowers are :
rows.solution:
A unisexual flower has either stamens or a pistil, not both. Papaya and watermelon bear unisexual flowers, while *Hibiscus* and mustard flowers are bisexual.

This is option (D) Watermelon and Papaya.

rows.stem: When an ‘X’ bearing sperm fertilises the egg, the resulting zygote has the following combination of chromosomes :
rows.solution:
A human egg always carries 22 autosomes and an X chromosome (22 + X). An X-bearing sperm also carries 22 + X. Their fusion gives a zygote with 44 autosomes and two X chromosomes, 44 + XX, which develops into a girl.

This is option (A) 44 + XX.

rows.stem: An object is placed in front of a convex mirror at infinity. According to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, the sign of the focal length and the sign of the image distance in this case are respectively :
rows.solution:
For a convex mirror the principal focus lies behind the mirror, on the side opposite to the incident light, so its focal length is positive. An object at infinity forms an image at the focus, also behind the mirror, so the image distance is positive too.

This is option (D) \(+\), \(+\).

rows.stem: For verifying Ohm’s law, we design an electric circuit diagram in which we show the arrangement of different circuit components. We find that with respect to the resistor, the :

options.label: A
options.text: ammeter is connected in parallel and the voltmeter in series.

options.label: B
options.text: ammeter is connected in series and the voltmeter in parallel.

options.label: C
options.text: ammeter and voltmeter are both connected in series.

options.label: D
options.text: ammeter and voltmeter are both connected in parallel.

rows.solution:
The ammeter must carry the whole current through the resistor, so it is connected in series with it. The voltmeter measures the potential difference across the resistor, so it is connected in parallel with it.

This is option (B) ammeter is connected in series and the voltmeter in parallel.

rows.stem: In a resistive circuit if the current is increased to two times, the percentage change in the amount of heat dissipated in the circuit would be :
rows.solution:
By Joule's law of heating, \(H = I^2Rt\). If the current becomes \(2I\), the heat becomes \((2I)^2Rt = 4I^2Rt = 4H\).

The increase is \(4H - H = 3H\), so the percentage change is \(\dfrac{3H}{H} \times 100 = 300\%\).

This is option (B) 300%.

rows.stem: A positron enters a uniform magnetic field at right angles to it as shown. The direction of force experienced by the positron will be :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the directions are given only in the drawing: four parallel arrowed lines labelled 'Magnetic field' and one arrowed line crossing them at right angles labelled 'Positron'. The direction of each arrow is the data the question turns on and is withheld here. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
In the figure the magnetic field points to the right across the page and the positron moves up the page, at right angles to it. A positron carries a positive charge, so its motion is equivalent to a current in its direction of motion.

By Fleming's left-hand rule: forefinger along the field (to the right), middle finger along the current (up the page); the thumb then points into the page.

This is option (C) into the page.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Sodium oxide is an amphoteric oxide.

**Reason (R) :** Metal oxides which react with both acids as well as bases are known as amphoteric oxides.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Sodium oxide is a basic oxide: it reacts with acids to form a salt and water and dissolves in water to give sodium hydroxide, but it does not react with bases. So the Assertion is false. Metal oxides that react with both acids and bases to give salt and water are indeed called amphoteric oxides (aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are examples), so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** When a bacterium divides into two, and the resultant two bacteria divide again, the four bacteria produced would be almost similar.

**Reason (R) :** DNA copying involves small inaccuracies in the reproduction process.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
When a bacterium divides by binary fission, its DNA is copied and each daughter cell gets a copy. The copying is not perfectly accurate, so the four bacteria produced after two divisions are very similar but not identical: the Assertion is true.

The Reason, that DNA copying involves small inaccuracies, is true, and it is exactly why the bacteria are only almost similar.

The Reason is true and explains the Assertion. This is option (A).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** A person suffering from myopia cannot see the distant objects clearly.

**Reason (R) :** A converging lens is used for the correction of myopic eye as it can form real as well as virtual images of the objects placed in front of it.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina, so a myopic person cannot see distant objects clearly. The Assertion is true.

Myopia is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power, not a converging lens. So the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Magnetic field lines do not intersect each other.

**Reason (R) :** Magnetic field lines are imaginary lines, the tangent to which at any point gives the direction of the field at that point.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Magnetic field lines never intersect, because at a point of intersection the field would have two directions at once, and a compass needle placed there would have to point two ways, which is impossible. The Assertion is true.

Field lines are imaginary lines, and the tangent at any point gives the direction of the field there, so the Reason is true. The marking scheme takes the Reason as not explaining the Assertion, since it does not state that the direction at a point is unique. (The other reading can be argued: the Reason is the premise of the argument above, since a single tangent at each point means a single direction, so a student could defend that it explains the Assertion.)

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem: What is observed when aqueous solutions of potassium iodide and lead nitrate are mixed together ? Name the type of reaction and write the chemical equation for the reaction that occurs.
rows.solution:
A yellow precipitate of lead iodide is formed.

This is a double displacement reaction (a precipitation reaction): the ions of the two compounds are exchanged.

\(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2(aq) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow PbI_2(s) + 2KNO_3(aq)}\)

rows.stem:
When copper powder is heated in a watch glass, a black substance is formed.

(i) Why is this black substance formed ? Name it.

(ii) How can this black substance be reversed to its original form ?
rows.solution:
(i) On heating, copper combines with the oxygen of the air, that is, copper is oxidised. The black substance is copper(II) oxide, CuO.

\(\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2CuO}\)

(ii) Pass hydrogen gas over the heated black copper oxide. The oxide is reduced to copper, and the black coating turns brown again.

\(\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Cu + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(a) Why is it important to prevent oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing in birds and mammals ?

(b) Which animals can tolerate some mixing of the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood streams ? On what factor does the body temperature of these animals depend ?
rows.solution:
(a) Birds and mammals have high energy needs, because they constantly use energy to maintain their body temperature. Keeping oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate allows a highly efficient supply of oxygen to the body, which meets these needs.

(b) Amphibians and many reptiles, which have three-chambered hearts, tolerate some mixing. Their body temperature depends on the temperature of the environment.

rows.stem:
Mendel crossed a pure tall pea plant (TT) with a pure short pea plant (tt) and obtained all tall plants in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation.

(a) What is the gene combination present in the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation ?

(b) Give reason why only tall plants are observed in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny.

(c) What will be the ratio of the plants obtained in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation when \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated ?
rows.solution:
(a) Every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant receives T from the tall parent and t from the short parent, so its gene combination is Tt.

(b) Tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t). In a Tt plant only the dominant trait is expressed, so all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are tall.

(c) Selfing Tt gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1, so in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation tall : short = 3 : 1.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: When and where does a rainbow appear in the sky ? Draw a labelled ray diagram to show its formation.
rows.solution:
A rainbow appears in the sky after a rain shower, and it is always formed in the direction opposite to that of the sun.

Diagram: draw a ray of sunlight falling on a spherical raindrop. At entry it is refracted and dispersed into its colours; at the back of the drop it is reflected internally; on leaving the drop it is refracted again. Show the emerging rays spread out, and label the sunlight, the raindrop, and the red and violet rays. Draw arrows on the rays to show their direction.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: What is scattering of light ? Why does the clear sky appear blue ?
rows.solution:
Scattering of light is the change in the direction of light caused by the particles (molecules or fine colloidal particles) in its path.

The molecules of air and other fine particles in the atmosphere are smaller than the wavelength of visible light. They scatter light of shorter wavelength (the blue end) much more strongly than light of longer wavelength (red). When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions, so the clear sky appears blue.

rows.stem: V – I graph for two conducting wires A and B are as shown. If both wires are of the same length and same diameter, which of the two is made of a material of high resistivity ? Give reasons to justify your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the answer is read off the printed graph: V on the vertical axis and I on the horizontal, no tick values, two straight lines from the origin labelled A and B. Their relative slopes are the quantity under test and are withheld here. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
Wire B is made of the material of higher resistivity.

In a V-I graph with V on the vertical axis, the slope \(\dfrac{V}{I}\) is the resistance R. The line for B is steeper than the line for A, so B has the greater resistance.

\(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\), and both wires have the same length and the same diameter (so the same area of cross-section). So the resistivity \(\rho\) is proportional to R, and the wire of greater resistance, B, has the greater resistivity.

rows.stem: We do not clean ponds or lakes but an aquarium needs to be cleaned regularly. Why ?
rows.solution:
Ponds and lakes are natural ecosystems. They have natural cleansing agents, the decomposers (bacteria and fungi), which break down dead matter and wastes, so they do not need to be cleaned.

An aquarium is a man-made ecosystem without such decomposers, so the wastes keep accumulating in it, and it needs to be cleaned periodically.

rows.stem:
Silver chloride kept in a china dish turns grey in sunlight.

(a) Write the colour of silver chloride when it was kept in the china dish.

(b) Name the type of chemical reaction taking place and write the chemical equation for the reaction.

(c) State one use of the reaction. Name one more chemical which can be used for the same purpose.
rows.solution:
(a) Silver chloride is white.

(b) It is a decomposition reaction, brought about by light (photolytic decomposition). Silver chloride splits into grey silver and chlorine gas:

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

(c) Such reactions are used in black and white photography. Silver bromide can be used for the same purpose:

\(\mathrm{2AgBr(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Br_2(g)}\)

rows.stem: With the help of suitable chemical equations, list the two main differences between roasting and calcination. How is metal reduced from the product obtained after roasting/calcination of the ore ? Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.
rows.solution:
Differences between roasting and calcination:

1. Roasting is carried out for sulphide ores; calcination is carried out for carbonate ores.

2. In roasting the ore is heated strongly in excess of air; in calcination it is heated strongly in limited air or in the absence of air.

Roasting of zinc blende:

\(\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

Calcination of calamine:

\(\mathrm{ZnCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} ZnO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

(So roasting gives off sulphur dioxide, while calcination gives off carbon dioxide.)

Both processes give the metal oxide, which is then reduced to the metal with a suitable reducing agent such as carbon (coke):

\(\mathrm{ZnO(s) + C(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Zn(s) + CO(g)}\)

(For metals low in the reactivity series, heating alone is enough: \(\mathrm{2HgO(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2Hg(l) + O_2(g)}\), or for copper, \(\mathrm{2Cu_2O + Cu_2S \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 6Cu(s) + SO_2(g)}\).)

rows.stem:
(i) What is the first step in the breakdown of glucose during aerobic and anaerobic respiration ? Where does it take place ?

(ii) ATP is called the energy currency of the cell. Why ?

(iii) What is meant by “residual volume of air” in a breathing cycle ?
rows.solution:
(i) The first step in both is the breakdown of glucose, a six-carbon molecule, into pyruvate (pyruvic acid), a three-carbon molecule. It takes place in the cytoplasm.

(ii) The energy released during respiration is used to make ATP. Whenever a cell needs energy for any activity, ATP is broken down to give a fixed amount of energy, which drives the energy-requiring (endothermic) reactions in the cell. Because cells use it like money for every activity, ATP is called the energy currency of the cell.

(iii) Even after we breathe out, the lungs always contain some air. This is the residual volume of air. It ensures that there is enough time for oxygen to be absorbed into the blood and for carbon dioxide to be released.

rows.stem: Write in sequence the steps for experimental verification of the fact that “sunlight is essential for photosynthesis”.
rows.solution:
1. Take a potted plant and keep it in the dark for about a day (two or three days is safer), so that the starch already present in its leaves is used up (destarching).

2. Cover a part of one leaf on both sides with strips of black paper, so that this part gets no sunlight.

3. Keep the plant in sunlight for several hours (a whole day).

4. Pluck the leaf and remove the black paper. Boil the leaf in water and then in alcohol (on a water bath) to remove the chlorophyll, and wash it.

5. Dip the leaf in dilute iodine solution to test for starch.

6. Observation: the part that was covered shows no blue-black colour, so no starch was made there; the rest of the leaf turns blue-black, showing that starch was made. So sunlight is essential for photosynthesis.

rows.stem: Name the hormone released and the gland which secretes it in human beings during scary situations. How does the body respond to enable it to deal with the situation ?
rows.solution:
The hormone is adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands.

It is secreted directly into the blood and carried to different parts of the body. Any two responses:

1. The heart beats faster, so more oxygen is supplied to the muscles.

2. The breathing rate increases, because of faster contractions of the diaphragm and the rib muscles.

3. The blood supply to the digestive system and the skin is reduced.

4. Blood is diverted to the skeletal muscles.

Together these prepare the body to deal with the situation.

rows.stem:
A student has focussed the image of an object of height 3 cm on a white screen using a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. If the distance of the object from the mirror is 18 cm, find the values of the following :

(i) Distance of the image from the mirror

(ii) Height of the image
rows.solution:
The image is on a screen, so it is real and the mirror formula applies with \(h = +3\) cm, \(f = -12\) cm and \(u = -18\) cm.

(i) \(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{18} = \dfrac{-3 + 2}{36} = -\dfrac{1}{36}\).

\(v = -36\) cm: the image is 36 cm in front of the mirror.

(ii) \(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = -\dfrac{v}{u}\), so \(h' = -\dfrac{v}{u} \times h = -\dfrac{-36}{-18} \times 3 = -6\) cm.

The image is 6 cm high, real and inverted.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: Define power of a lens. The focal length of a lens is \(-10\) cm. Write the nature of the lens and find its power. If an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, according to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, what will be the sign of magnification in this case ?
rows.solution:
The power of a lens is the degree of convergence or divergence of light rays achieved by it. It is the reciprocal of its focal length in metres, \(P = \dfrac{1}{f}\), and its unit is the dioptre (D).

A focal length of \(-10\) cm is negative, so the lens is a concave (diverging) lens.

\(P = \dfrac{100}{f\ (\text{in cm})} = \dfrac{100}{-10} = -10\) D.

A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect image, so the magnification is positive. (With \(u = -20\) cm: \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{3}{20}\), so \(v = -\dfrac{20}{3}\) cm and \(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = +\dfrac{1}{3}\).)

rows.stem: Explain the meaning of overloading of an electrical circuit. List two possible causes due to which overloading may occur in household circuits. Write one preventive measure that should be taken to avoid overloading of domestic circuits.
rows.solution:
Overloading happens when an excessive current is drawn through the wires of a circuit, more than they are rated to carry. The wires heat up and may cause a fire.

Any two causes: the live wire and the neutral wire coming into direct contact (short-circuiting); connecting too many appliances to a single socket; an accidental hike in the supply voltage.

Preventive measure (any one): use a fuse (or a circuit breaker) of proper rating in the circuit; do not connect too many appliances to a single socket; use wires of proper rating and insulation.

rows.stem: Explain how some harmful chemicals enter our bodies through the food chain. Why is the concentration of these harmful chemicals found to be maximum in human beings ?
rows.solution:
Pesticides and other chemicals are used to protect crops. They are washed down into the soil or into water bodies. From the soil and water they are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and from water bodies they are taken up by aquatic plants and animals. When we eat these plants and animals (cereals, vegetables, fish), the chemicals enter our bodies through the food chain.

These chemicals are not degradable, so they accumulate progressively at each trophic level (biological magnification). Human beings occupy the top level in any food chain, so the maximum concentration of these chemicals accumulates in our bodies.

rows.stem: An acid ‘X’ and an alcohol ‘Y’ react with each other in the presence of an acid catalyst to form a sweet smelling substance ‘Z’. Identify ‘X’, ‘Y’ and ‘Z’. Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved and name it. The substance ‘Z’ on treatment with sodium hydroxide produces back the alcohol ‘Y’ and sodium ethanoate. Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved and name it, giving justification for the name.
rows.solution:
'X' is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\); 'Y' is ethanol, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\); 'Z' is the sweet-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate, \(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5}\).

The reaction is esterification:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

With sodium hydroxide, the ester is converted back to the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow C_2H_5OH + CH_3COONa}\)

This is called saponification, because the same reaction of an alkali with esters (fats and oils) is used in the preparation of soap.

rows.stem:
(i) Name the simplest saturated hydrocarbon. Draw its electron dot structure. Which type of bonds exist in this compound ?

(ii) Name any two mixtures of the carbon compound used as a fuel in daily life, of which the above mentioned compound is an important component.

(iii) In which homologous series of carbon compounds can this compound be placed ? Write the general formula of the series.

(iv) Which type of flame is produced on burning it ?
rows.solution:
(i) The simplest saturated hydrocarbon is methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\).

Electron dot structure: the carbon atom, with 4 valence electrons, is at the centre, and four hydrogen atoms surround it. Carbon shares one pair of electrons (one electron of its own and one of the hydrogen) with each hydrogen atom. Carbon then has eight electrons around it and each hydrogen two.

The bonds are single covalent bonds.

(ii) Biogas and CNG (compressed natural gas).

(iii) It belongs to the alkanes, general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\).

(iv) Being saturated, it burns with a clean blue flame.

rows.stem:
(i) List three points of difference between nervous and hormonal mechanisms for control and coordination in animals.

(ii) How are auxins related with the bending of plant shoot towards unidirectional light ? Explain.
rows.solution:
(i) Any three differences:

| Nervous control | Hormonal control |
|---|---|
| Messages are sent as electrical impulses | Messages are carried as chemicals (hormones) |
| Carried through neurons (nerve fibres) | Carried through the blood |
| Produces rapid responses | Produces slow responses |
| Responses are short-lived | Responses are long-lasting |

(ii) Auxin is synthesised at the tip of the shoot. When light falls on the shoot from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shaded side. The higher concentration of auxin makes the cells on the shaded side grow longer, so that side grows more and the shoot bends towards the light.

rows.stem:
(i) Name the disorder which a person is likely to suffer from due to the following :

(I) Over-secretion of growth hormone

(II) Deficiency of oestrogen in females

(III) Less secretion of thyroxine

Also name the gland that secretes each of the hormones mentioned above.

(ii) How is the timing and amount of hormone released regulated ? Explain with the help of an example.
rows.solution:
(i)

| Hormone condition | Disorder | Gland |
|---|---|---|
| (I) Over-secretion of growth hormone | Gigantism | Pituitary |
| (II) Deficiency of oestrogen | Delayed puberty (the female secondary sexual characters do not develop properly) | Ovary |
| (III) Less secretion of thyroxine | Goitre | Thyroid |

(ii) The timing and amount of hormone released are regulated by feedback mechanisms.

Example: if the sugar level in the blood rises, it is detected by the cells of the pancreas, which respond by producing more insulin. As the blood sugar level falls, insulin secretion is reduced.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
(a) An object is placed in front of a convex lens of focal length f. If the distance of the object from the lens is 2f, draw a ray diagram to show the formation of the image. Write the value of magnification in this case.

(b) A student has focussed the image of a candle flame on a white screen using a convex lens. The situation is as given below :

Length of the flame = 2 cm

Focal length of the lens = 12 cm

Distance of the flame from the lens = 16 cm

If the flame is perpendicular to the principal axis of the lens, calculate the values of the following :

(i) Distance of the image from the lens

(ii) Length of the image formed
rows.solution:
(a) Ray diagram with the object AB at \(2\mathrm{F_1}\): from the top A draw a ray parallel to the principal axis, which after refraction passes through the focus \(\mathrm{F_2}\) on the other side. Draw a second ray from A through the optical centre O, which goes straight on without bending. The two refracted rays meet below the axis at A', and the image A'B' forms at \(2\mathrm{F_2}\). Mark arrows on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are missing.

The image is real, inverted and of the same size as the object, so the magnification is \(m = -1\).

(b) The image is on a screen, so it is real. Here \(u = -16\) cm, \(f = +12\) cm and \(h = +2\) cm.

(i) By the lens formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{f} = -\dfrac{1}{16} + \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{-3 + 4}{48} = \dfrac{1}{48}\), so \(v = +48\) cm.

The image is 48 cm from the lens, on the other side.

(ii) \(h' = \dfrac{v}{u} \times h = \dfrac{+48}{-16} \times 2 = -6\) cm.

The image of the flame is 6 cm long, real and inverted.

rows.stem: For the solutions provided, which group is/are likely to have pH value (i) less than 7, and (ii) greater than 7 ?
rows.context:
The teacher while conducting practicals in the laboratory divided the students into three groups and gave them various solutions to find out their pH and classify them into acidic, basic and neutral solutions.

Group A – Lemon juice, vinegar, colourless aerated drink

Group B – Tomato juice, coffee, ginger juice

Group C – Sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, lime water
rows.solution:
(i) Groups A and B: lemon juice, vinegar, aerated drink, tomato juice, coffee and ginger juice are all acidic, so their pH is less than 7.

(ii) Group C: sodium hydroxide and lime water are bases, so their pH is greater than 7. (Sodium chloride in the same group is a neutral salt, with pH 7.)

rows.stem: List two ways of determining pH of a solution
rows.context:
The teacher while conducting practicals in the laboratory divided the students into three groups and gave them various solutions to find out their pH and classify them into acidic, basic and neutral solutions.

Group A – Lemon juice, vinegar, colourless aerated drink

Group B – Tomato juice, coffee, ginger juice

Group C – Sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, lime water
rows.solution: Using pH paper, and using a universal indicator, and matching the colour with the pH colour chart. (A pH meter can also be used.)

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Explain, why the sour substances such as lemon juice are effective in cleaning the tarnished copper vessels.
rows.context:
The teacher while conducting practicals in the laboratory divided the students into three groups and gave them various solutions to find out their pH and classify them into acidic, basic and neutral solutions.

Group A – Lemon juice, vinegar, colourless aerated drink

Group B – Tomato juice, coffee, ginger juice

Group C – Sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, lime water
rows.solution:
A copper vessel becomes tarnished because its surface reacts with the moist air to form a dull coating of basic copper compounds (copper oxide and basic copper carbonate). This coating is basic.

Lemon juice is acidic. Its acid neutralises the basic coating, forming a soluble salt that is washed away with water, so the shine of the copper is restored.

rows.stem: “pH has great importance in our daily life.” Justify this statement by giving two examples.
rows.context:
The teacher while conducting practicals in the laboratory divided the students into three groups and gave them various solutions to find out their pH and classify them into acidic, basic and neutral solutions.

Group A – Lemon juice, vinegar, colourless aerated drink

Group B – Tomato juice, coffee, ginger juice

Group C – Sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, lime water
rows.solution:
Any two examples:

1. Digestion: our stomach produces hydrochloric acid, and digestion needs the right pH there. Excess acid causes indigestion and pain, which is relieved by an antacid such as milk of magnesia.

2. Tooth decay: when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5, the tooth enamel (calcium phosphate) is corroded. Toothpastes, which are basic, neutralise the excess acid.

3. Self-defence by animals and plants: a bee sting injects an acid that causes pain, and rubbing a mild base such as baking soda on it gives relief.

4. Aquatic life: when the pH of river water is lowered (for example by acid rain), the survival of aquatic life becomes difficult.

rows.stem: Name the type of fission that occurs in Leishmania and Plasmodium.
rows.context:
All the reproductive methods of living organisms are broadly categorized into two types : 1. Asexual reproduction, and 2. Sexual reproduction.

Asexual reproduction involves the participation of a single parent without the formation of gametes, fertilisation and transfer of genetic material. This method is a common means of rapidly increasing offsprings under favourable conditions.
rows.solution: *Leishmania* reproduces by binary fission, and *Plasmodium* by multiple fission.

rows.stem: Write one advantage of sexual mode of reproduction over asexual reproduction.
rows.context:
All the reproductive methods of living organisms are broadly categorized into two types : 1. Asexual reproduction, and 2. Sexual reproduction.

Asexual reproduction involves the participation of a single parent without the formation of gametes, fertilisation and transfer of genetic material. This method is a common means of rapidly increasing offsprings under favourable conditions.
rows.solution: Sexual reproduction produces more variation in the offspring, and variation is useful for ensuring the survival of a species.

rows.stem:
Give reasons why :

(i) Colonies of yeast fail to multiply in water but multiply in sugar solution.

(ii) Rhizopus individuals do not grow on a dry slice of bread.
rows.context:
All the reproductive methods of living organisms are broadly categorized into two types : 1. Asexual reproduction, and 2. Sexual reproduction.

Asexual reproduction involves the participation of a single parent without the formation of gametes, fertilisation and transfer of genetic material. This method is a common means of rapidly increasing offsprings under favourable conditions.
rows.solution:
(i) Yeast needs nutrients to grow and multiply. A sugar solution provides it with food and energy, so it multiplies by budding; plain water provides no nutrients.

(ii) *Rhizopus* needs moisture (as well as nutrients) to grow. A dry slice of bread has no moisture, so its spores do not grow.

rows.stem: Name the filamentous structures a student could identify when he collected water from a pond that appeared dark green. How do these organisms multiply ? Explain.
rows.context:
All the reproductive methods of living organisms are broadly categorized into two types : 1. Asexual reproduction, and 2. Sexual reproduction.

Asexual reproduction involves the participation of a single parent without the formation of gametes, fertilisation and transfer of genetic material. This method is a common means of rapidly increasing offsprings under favourable conditions.
rows.solution:
The filamentous structures are *Spirogyra*, a green alga.

They multiply by fragmentation: on maturing, the *Spirogyra* filament simply breaks up into smaller pieces (fragments), and each fragment grows into a new individual.

rows.stem: What is the relationship between the readings of \(\mathrm{A_1}\) and \(\mathrm{A_3}\) ? Give reasons for your answer.
rows.context: Consider the following electrical circuit diagram in which nine identical resistors of \(3\,\Omega\) each are connected as shown. If the reading of the ammeter \(\mathrm{A_1}\) is 1 ampere, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit exists only as a drawing: a battery, a plug key, ammeters \(\mathrm{A_1}\), \(\mathrm{A_2}\), \(\mathrm{A_3}\), voltmeters \(\mathrm{V_1}\), \(\mathrm{V_2}\) and nine \(3\,\Omega\) resistors drawn in three groups. How the resistors are grouped and where each meter sits is what every sub-part turns on and is withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
The readings of \(\mathrm{A_1}\) and \(\mathrm{A_3}\) are the same: both read 1 A.

Both ammeters are connected in series in the main line of the circuit, and the same current flows through every part of a series circuit.

rows.stem: What is the relationship between the readings of \(\mathrm{A_2}\) and \(\mathrm{A_3}\) ?
rows.context: Consider the following electrical circuit diagram in which nine identical resistors of \(3\,\Omega\) each are connected as shown. If the reading of the ammeter \(\mathrm{A_1}\) is 1 ampere, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit exists only as a drawing: a battery, a plug key, ammeters \(\mathrm{A_1}\), \(\mathrm{A_2}\), \(\mathrm{A_3}\), voltmeters \(\mathrm{V_1}\), \(\mathrm{V_2}\) and nine \(3\,\Omega\) resistors drawn in three groups. How the resistors are grouped and where each meter sits is what every sub-part turns on and is withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
The ammeter \(\mathrm{A_2}\) is in one of the four identical \(3\,\Omega\) branches of the last parallel group, so the current of 1 A divides equally among the four branches.

The reading of \(\mathrm{A_2}\) is \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of the reading of \(\mathrm{A_3}\), that is \(0{\cdot}25\) A.

rows.stem: Determine the reading of the voltmeter \(\mathrm{V_1}\).
rows.context: Consider the following electrical circuit diagram in which nine identical resistors of \(3\,\Omega\) each are connected as shown. If the reading of the ammeter \(\mathrm{A_1}\) is 1 ampere, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit exists only as a drawing: a battery, a plug key, ammeters \(\mathrm{A_1}\), \(\mathrm{A_2}\), \(\mathrm{A_3}\), voltmeters \(\mathrm{V_1}\), \(\mathrm{V_2}\) and nine \(3\,\Omega\) resistors drawn in three groups. How the resistors are grouped and where each meter sits is what every sub-part turns on and is withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
The voltmeter \(\mathrm{V_1}\) is across the first group, two \(3\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel:

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), so \(R_p = \dfrac{3}{2}\,\Omega\).

The whole current of 1 A flows through this group, so by \(V = IR\),

\(V_1 = 1 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}\) V \(= 1{\cdot}5\) V.

rows.stem: Find the total resistance of the circuit.
rows.context: Consider the following electrical circuit diagram in which nine identical resistors of \(3\,\Omega\) each are connected as shown. If the reading of the ammeter \(\mathrm{A_1}\) is 1 ampere, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit exists only as a drawing: a battery, a plug key, ammeters \(\mathrm{A_1}\), \(\mathrm{A_2}\), \(\mathrm{A_3}\), voltmeters \(\mathrm{V_1}\), \(\mathrm{V_2}\) and nine \(3\,\Omega\) resistors drawn in three groups. How the resistors are grouped and where each meter sits is what every sub-part turns on and is withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
The three groups are in series.

First group, two \(3\,\Omega\) in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_{p_1}} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(R_{p_1} = \dfrac{3}{2}\,\Omega\).

Second group, three \(3\,\Omega\) in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_{p_2}} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(R_{p_2} = 1\,\Omega\).

Third group, four \(3\,\Omega\) in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R_{p_3}} = \dfrac{4}{3}\), so \(R_{p_3} = \dfrac{3}{4}\,\Omega\).

Total resistance: \(R = \dfrac{3}{2} + 1 + \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{13}{4}\,\Omega = 3{\cdot}25\,\Omega\).
